note: WORKTREE-TAKE CAN HAND THE SAME POOL SLOT TO TWO SESSIONS, AND THE LOSER GETS A SILENT EMPTY DIRECTORY RATHER THAN AN ERROR. Observed 2026-08-16. I ran make worktree-take NAME=the-palimpsest; it created branch campaign/the-palimpsest and gave me a populated worktree, which I verified by reading files out of it (windows/hearsay/src and tests both read fine). Minutes later a parallel take of NAME=the-burr repointed that same physical slot: git worktree list then showed the-burr at campaign/the-burr and NO the-palimpsest entry, while the path .claude/worktrees/the-palimpsest survived as a PLAIN DIRECTORY with no .git in it. THE FAILURE MODE IS THE DANGEROUS PART: git commands run inside that orphan path walk UP to the main checkout and answer from it, so git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD had earlier printed campaign/the-palimpsest but git status later printed On branch main, working tree clean. A scoped crate build there failed with the message no test target named X, which reads like a missing Cargo.toml entry and is really a missing checkout. THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATOR is git ls-files piped to wc -l: 0 tracked files means the path is not a worktree at all, whatever git rev-parse says. Recovery that worked: remove the orphan directory, then git worktree add .claude/worktrees/NAME campaign/NAME against the branch the take already created. Cost is a cold target dir. I did not touch the-burr; it belongs to whoever took it.
